chapter.title: Toys, Games and Sports Equipment; Parts and Accessories Thereof

page.h1: HTS Chapter 95: Toys, Games and Sports Equipment; Parts and Accessories Thereof — U.S. Export FAQ

seo.title: U.S. Toy & Sports Gear Export FAQ: Canada Tariffs, HS Codes
seo.shortDescription: Short answers: does Canada tariff U.S. toys, golf clubs, consoles or gym gear (50% on listed lines)? Mexico, China and EU rates, and HS codes.
keywords: tariffs on trading cards usa to canada

intro: Short answers to what people search about exporting U.S. toys, video game consoles, cards, sports and exercise equipment and fishing tackle, each drawn from the other export pages of this report.
keyTakeaways: Canada charges 50% on U.S. video game consoles, exercise machines, other sports gear, golf parts and fishing rods since September 8, 2026; toys, cards, complete golf clubs and golf balls still enter free under CUSMA.
Mexico (USMCA), the EU (since July 1, 2026), Australia (AUSFTA) and South Korea (KORUS) let U.S. Chapter 95 goods in free; China adds 10% to its normal rate.
Most Chapter 95 goods are EAR99; the HS code, the first six digits of the Schedule B number, is 9503.00 for toys, 9504.50 for video game consoles, 9504.40 for cards and 9506 for sports gear.
questionSource: Google search suggestions (suggestqueries.google.com, November 20, 2026) for queries such as "canada tariff on us toys", "are there tariffs on toys from usa to canada", "canada tariffs on golf", "duty on golf clubs from usa to canada", "canada tariff video game consoles", "canada tariff exercise equipment", "canada tariffs sports equipment", "tariff on trading cards", "pokemon cards tariff", "mexico arancel juguetes", "does mexico have tariffs on us goods", "does china have tariffs on us goods", "eu tariffs on us goods", "uk tariffs on us goods", "japan tariffs on us goods", "australia tariffs on us goods", "hs code for toys", "hs code video game console", "hs code golf clubs", "hs code exercise equipment", "hs code trading cards", "do i need an export license", "eccn for toys" and "toy exports".

faqs.question: Does Canada have tariffs on U.S. toys?
faqs.answer: No, not today. Toys, dolls, puzzles and models (9503) are not on Canada's September 8, 2026 counter-tariff list, and U.S. toys that qualify under CUSMA enter free (Canada's normal rate is free except 8% on wheeled ride-on toys). Canada did charge 25% on U.S. toys from March 13 to August 31, 2025.
searchedAs: are there tariffs on toys from us to canada
canada tariffs on us goods list

faqs.question: Is there duty on golf clubs from the USA to Canada?
faqs.answer: Complete golf clubs (9506.31) and golf balls (9506.32) pay nothing: they are free under Canada's normal rate and CUSMA and are not on its 2026 surtax list. Other golf equipment (9506.39), such as club heads and shafts, pays a 50% surtax on U.S.-origin goods since September 8, 2026.

is there duty on golf clubs from usa to canada
duty on golf clubs from usa to canada

faqs.question: Does Canada tariff U.S. video game consoles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since September 8, 2026 Canada's United States Surtax Order (2026) charges 50% on U.S.-origin video game consoles and machines and their controllers, parts and accessories (9504.50), with no CUSMA exemption. Coin-operated games, playing and trading cards and billiards are not listed.

faqs.question: Does Canada have tariffs on U.S. sports and exercise equipment?
faqs.answer: On much of it, yes. Since September 8, 2026 Canada charges 50% on U.S. exercise equipment such as treadmills, exercise bikes and weights (9506.91), other sports and outdoor-game equipment such as hockey gear and swimming pools (9506.99) and fishing rods. A $1 million shipment of U.S. treadmills now pays $500,000, against nothing in January 2025. Skis, rackets, balls, skates, golf clubs and golf balls are not listed.

faqs.question: Are there Canadian tariffs on U.S. trading cards?
faqs.answer: Not today. Playing and trading cards (9504.40) are free under Canada's normal rate and CUSMA and are not on the September 8, 2026 list. They paid Canada's 25% counter-tariff from March 4 to August 31, 2025.
searchedAs: tariffs on trading cards usa to canada

faqs.question: Does Mexico charge tariffs on U.S. toys?
faqs.answer: Not on U.S. toys that qualify under USMCA: they enter Mexico free, and Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. goods. From January 1, 2026 Mexico raised its general rate on almost every toy line, playing cards and other party articles to 30%, from 15% or free, so goods that fail the USMCA origin rules now pay much more.

does mexico charge tariffs on us goods

faqs.question: Does China have tariffs on U.S. toys and sports goods?
faqs.answer: Yes. China's normal rate is 0% on toys and video game consoles and 6% on most sports equipment, but it adds a 10% extra tariff to every U.S. good, so a $1 million shipment of U.S. consoles or toys pays $100,000. The extra tariff would rise to 34% if China's suspension ends on January 10, 2027, and China's 2019 counter-tariffs apply to buyers without an exclusion after December 31, 2026.

does china have tariffs on us products
does china charge tariffs on us goods

faqs.question: What do the EU, the UK, Japan and Australia charge on U.S. toys and sports gear?
faqs.answer: Since July 1, 2026 the EU charges 0% on every U.S. Chapter 95 good under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, until December 31, 2029 (up to 4.7% before). The UK charges 0–4% under its Global Tariff, with consoles free. Japan lets toys, consoles and most sports gear in free and charges 3.2% on cards, balls, festive goods and tackle, and Australia is free for qualifying U.S. goods under AUSFTA.

does australia have tariffs on us goods

faqs.question: What is the HS code for toys, golf clubs, exercise equipment and trading cards?
faqs.answer: Toys, dolls, puzzles and models are all 9503.00. Complete golf clubs are 9506.31, golf balls 9506.32 and other golf equipment such as heads and shafts 9506.39; exercise and gym equipment is 9506.91; playing and trading cards are 9504.40. These six digits are also the start of the 10-digit Schedule B number used for U.S. export filing.
searchedAs: hs code for toys and games

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a video game console or controller?
faqs.answer: Video game consoles and handhelds, with their controllers, parts and accessories, are 9504.50. Coin- or card-operated arcade games and slot machines are 9504.30. Game software on discs or cartridges is not Chapter 95: it is classified with recorded media in 8523.
searchedAs: handheld video game console hs code

faqs.question: Do I need an export license for toys or video game consoles?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Most toys, games and sports goods are EAR99 and need no licence except for sanctioned destinations; toys (9503.00) need a BIS licence for Russia and Belarus. Consoles that use encryption may be classified 5A992.c (mass market), which ships licence-free to most countries. Slot machines need annual registration with the U.S. Attorney General under the Gambling Devices Act.

do i need export license in usa

faqs.question: How much do U.S. exports of toys, games and sports equipment total, and who buys them?
faqs.answer: The U.S. exported $6.71 billion of Chapter 95 goods in 2025, down 3.5%. Video game consoles and their parts ($1.28 billion) and toys ($1.17 billion) are the largest lines. Canada buys 38.7% and Mexico 13.7%, followed by the UK, Australia and Japan.
